rights: Author-hosted download is public. No blanket open license or redistribution authorization is inferred; original remains in temporary holdout.

notation.A: equilibrium partitions when player 1 proposes first
notation.B: equilibrium partitions when player 2 proposes first, still measured as player 1 share
notation.time: paper counts first accepted offer as T=1; worker may normalize it to t=0 if explicit
notation.P_E_P: induced equilibrium partition, not automatically a unique full strategy profile

original_model_and_assumptions.game: two players; divisible unit surplus; alternating unrestricted offers; responder accepts or rejects; rejection reverses proposer; no binding prior offers; perfect information; indefinite horizon
original_model_and_assumptions.strategy_space: history-dependent proposal and response maps at every finite history, including unreached histories
original_model_and_assumptions.outcomes: finite agreement (s,T), or perpetual disagreement (0,infinity), with disagreement separately ordered
original_model_and_assumptions.preference_base: complete, reflexive and transitive outcome ranking; common knowledge of preferences

formal_assumptions.content: strictly larger own share is better at the same date
positive share earlier is strictly better; every positive finite agreement outranks perpetual disagreement
one-period comparison invariant to common date shift
preference closedness/continuity in shares, including comparison with disagreement
required one-period compensating share increment weakly rises with own share

original_model_and_assumptions.numbering_caution: The introduction lists continuity as A-3 and stationarity as A-4; formal Section 2 reverses these labels. Evaluate content, not numbering alone.
original_model_and_assumptions.scope: preferences do not change with calendar time or history; time-dependent costs and nonlinear utility with additive fixed costs are outside this formulation (p.101 remark); incomplete-information bargaining is future work (pp.99-100)

equilibrium_concept.locator: Section 3 pp.101-103 (PDF5-7), P-1 through P-6 p.102
equilibrium_concept.concept: subgame perfect equilibrium: mutual best responses after every history, including accept/reject decisions and proposer continuation choices
equilibrium_concept.nash_comparison: unnumbered proposition p.101: every feasible partition is supportable as an ordinary Nash equilibrium; the p.103 example exposes a noncredible rejection
equilibrium_concept.evaluation_warning: Do not confuse subgame perfection with trembling-hand perfection; no assumption restricts all equilibria to stationary strategies.

conversion_maps.d1: d1(x)=smallest immediate player-1 share y weakly preferred by 1 to player-1 share x after one period; clipped at 0
conversion_maps.d2: d2(y)=largest immediate player-1 share x for which player 2 weakly prefers immediate x to delayed player-1 share y; clipped at 1

published_general_characterization.theorem: A=Delta1 != empty; B=Delta2 != empty; A and B closed intervals; B=A-epsilon for some epsilon>=0

proposition_map.label: Proposition 1
proposition_map.target: each fixed-point pair yields stationary credible strategies and partitions x in A,y in B

proposition_map.label: Proposition 2
proposition_map.target: Delta nonempty through continuity and a fixed point of d2 composed with d1

proposition_map.label: Proposition 3
proposition_map.target: Delta is a closed segment parallel to y=x, using A-5

proposition_map.label: Proposition 4
proposition_map.target: all equilibrium partitions lie in these projections; bounds use the deviation lemmas

published_general_characterization.supporting_lemmas: Lemmas 1-4 pp.103-104 (PDF7-8) relate proposer and responder continuation sets by credible rejection and profitable-deviation restrictions; Section 4 states only A-1/A-2 are needed there.

fixed_cost.preferences: own share minus c_i times elapsed periods, with separate disagreement ordering
fixed_cost.interior_domain_for_evaluation: 0<c1,c2<1; do not extrapolate the printed interior cases to costs exceeding the unit surplus

cases.timing: immediate stationary equilibria exist; history-dependent delay can also occur

fixed_cost.essential_counterexample: pp.107-108 (PDF11-12) explicitly construct an equal-cost equilibrium ending in period 2; the outcome need not be Pareto efficient. A blanket no-delay or unique-SPE claim for fixed costs fails.
fixed_cost.parameter_caution: The displayed Conclusion 1 does not spell out a bound on c_i. The clipped map characterization gives the appropriate feasible extension; evaluator must distinguish this issue from the printed interior cases.

geometric_discount.locator: Conclusion 2 and remarks p.108 (PDF12); proof p.109 (PDF13); model p.101
geometric_discount.timing_interior: agreement at first offer in every SPE
geometric_discount.symmetric: delta1=delta2=delta: starter share=1/(1+delta)>1/2; advantage vanishes as delta approaches 1
geometric_discount.comparative_statics: player 1 share rises with own patience delta1 and falls with opponent patience delta2; first-mover comparison must hold preferences fixed
geometric_discount.published_boundary_statement: at least one delta<1 and at least one delta>0; delta=0 is reserved for lexicographic priority for earlier agreement, not ordinary zero discount utility
geometric_discount.boundary_warning: both delta=1 and both delta=0 excluded from Conclusion 2; interior uniqueness/no-delay proof must not be applied without argument when a delta is 1. Formula at delta1=delta2=1 is undefined.
geometric_discount.scope_warning: A finite-horizon backward-induction argument, equality of discount factors, or stationary-candidate equations alone do not establish the original infinite-horizon uniqueness result.

timing_logic.sufficient_condition: A intersection B empty implies no initial rejection in an SPE, since a delayed partition would have to belong to both sets
timing_logic.scope: holds for the interior unequal-cost and geometric-discount cases; equal costs admit overlap and delay; overlap alone is not a constructive proof of delay

evaluator_independent_checks.classification: curator reasoning/verification aids, not extra published claims

equal_cost_delayed_construction.initial_response: 2 accepts iff s<=0.1; otherwise rejects and enters a stationary continuation with player-1 responder share e(s), player-1 proposer share e(s)+0.1
equal_cost_delayed_construction.path: offer0.5 rejected; next offer gives player1 0.4 and is accepted
equal_cost_delayed_construction.verification: player1 initial acceptance deviations yield <=0.1, rejected deviations yield e(s)-0.1<=0.3; player2 rejection yields 1-e(s)-0.1>=1-s for s>0.1; continuation profiles satisfy the equal-cost fixed-point thresholds
equal_cost_delayed_construction.interpretation: separate history-dependent example sufficient to refute a universal no-delay claim; preserve source provenance if used in evaluation

proof_obligations: State preferences, perpetual-disagreement ranking, information, proposer order and feasible shares.
Specify proposals and acceptance rules after all histories and handle threshold indifference; verify both players' deviations, including rejected/off-path offers.
Establish equilibrium existence separately from uniqueness; a stationary construction alone proves existence.
For geometric discounts, bound outcomes across all SPE by infimum/supremum or equivalent contraction argument; do not assume stationarity to prove uniqueness.
For general preferences, prove the conversion maps and fixed-point characterization including exclusion of other equilibrium partitions.
Analyze both fixed-cost rankings and equal costs, with interval multiplicity and a credible delayed equilibrium.
Derive the unequal-discount case and first-mover comparison; state the domain and boundary limitations.
Support any universal immediate-agreement claim by a valid argument; distinguish outcome/partition uniqueness from full off-path strategy uniqueness.
Check perpetual disagreement and arbitrary-duration deviations, or establish the conditions for a valid one-shot-deviation principle.
Separate an analytically reviewed proof from a machine-checked proof; no Lean formal verification is available here.

evaluation_rules.full_reconstruction: Requires general characterization plus both special families and timing exceptions, not only the famous discount formula.
evaluation_rules.acceptable_alternative_proof: Different notation and independently derived proofs are acceptable when assumptions, quantifiers and conclusion scope match.
evaluation_rules.question_underdetermination: A one-sentence waiting-cost question does not uniquely identify exponential rather than additive or more general time preferences. A narrower internally correct paper should be scored as partial reconstruction, not fabricated theory.
critical_failures: universal unique equilibrium for equal fixed costs
universal no delay for equal fixed costs
stationary-only algebra labelled proof of uniqueness over all SPE
unqualified first mover gets more than half with unequal patience
undefined formula presented at both discounts equal 1
evaluation_rules.memory_limit: This is a famous textbook model. Source-access restrictions cannot establish absence of pretraining memory; evaluate proof execution and coverage, not scientific novelty.
